posts.title: A Pedestrian Was Killed by a Train in Merced. Two Intersections Blocked.
posts.caption:
Central Valley governance. Merced County spending. Administrative accountability.
A pedestrian was killed by a train in Merced on Nov 21, and the train sat blocking two intersections while crews responded. When a death stops a city, the questions start with the crossing itself. Who maintains it, who inspects it, and when was it last checked? A crossing is a system, and systems leave a record. The full breakdown is in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: Reel Vault If Part17 Facebook Long
posts.caption:
ILLEGALLY FIRED: I Asked Through Every Formal Channel. Every box they tell you to check, I checked. Personnel file requested, formal complaint filed, records requests sent — I did not go to social media first. The process produced nothing. No reason. No documentation. No answer. The formal process is not built to find the truth; it is built to protect the institution. So you exhaust it anyway, and you document everything — because when the process fails you, the paper trail is the only voice you have left. Full story on the Illegally Fired podcast. They gave you a process — did it give you the truth? Tell me below. 209Connect every Tuesday, link in bio, free
